# 4 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Brothers' Fraternal Love and Unity

---

**13:1** Were I to praise the endurance of those young men, the praise would be insufficient. For they despised the passions and conquered the torments.

**13:2** How shall I not praise also the magnanimity of the brothers and their noble obedience to the law?

**13:3** For just as the branches of a tree, though each has its own direction, are united at the root, so too these brothers were united in their devotion to the law.

**13:4** Having been educated in the same law and trained in the same virtues, they loved one another.

**13:5** Their common nature deepened their love, and the law strengthened it; and righteousness made it firmer still.

**13:6** The harmony of the brothers confirmed their courage, so that the tyrant was not able to divide them from one another.

**13:7** The first born encouraged the others, saying: Be courageous and noble, brothers.

**13:8** Remember that by the same God who created us, the law was given to us and our father Jacob lived in it and proved its truth.

**13:9** And the Almighty will not punish us who do not turn aside from the commandments of our fathers.

**13:10** The second said: Be courageous, brothers. For we are the sons of Abraham and we shall not be put to shame in any way.

**13:11** Now the third said to the others: Be courageous and noble, brothers, for we are fighting the battle of justice.

**13:12** And the fourth said: O brothers, do not be afraid of the man who kills the body but cannot destroy the soul.

**13:13** The fifth said: Brothers, this present time is short and our life is passing, but the name of those who die for virtue endures forever.

**13:14** The sixth said: Do not be overcome by grief, brothers, for death is a release from the pains of this present life.

**13:15** And the seventh, youngest of all, said: Do not fear, brothers; but be strong, for it is not worthy of your age and wisdom to be afraid of the man who kills the body.

**13:16** Then each of them, trusting in this reasoning, entered into the flames of torture in full confidence that he would never cease to live.

**13:17** What a marvelous thing! What praise is due these noble souls, who having overcome their passions and having conquered the fear of death, went forward to the altar of holy martyrdom!

**13:18** Did not the mother herself make this brave choice — she who chose the better death for her sons and thereby sealed their immortal victory?

**13:19** Is it not worthy of the most exalted praise that she endured the death of seven sons on one day and did not allow her spirit to be broken?

**13:20** For from her womb they came, and with her womb they were nurtured, and by her teaching and her love they were raised to the endurance of virtue — and in her heart she held them even as they died.
